chunks.content: # [Master Express Lesson 11] Apparel Display Class: Let Your 3D Clothing Shine! This document details techniques and procedures for creating 3D apparel displays using Close3D software, focusing on hanging clothes, making furniture pieces, adjusting models and textures, and rendering reflective surfaces. It covers technical workflows, software versions, modeling tips, material settings, and practical examples for 3D clothing and display design. --- ## Hanging Clothes on Virtual Shelves and Dressers This section explains how to hang 3D clothing on virtual shelves and dressers, including handling different dresser types and improving model quality for realistic rendering. - **Virtual Dressers**: Multiple dresser types are demonstrated, including ordinary dressers, pants dressers, belt dressers, and towel dressers. After hanging clothes, you can manipulate and pull the dresser to check fit and positioning. - **Surface Diameter Adjustment**: When finalizing the dresser model for rendering, set the surface diameter to zero to enhance quality. - **Border Plates**: Adding small plates along the dresser borders improves realism and detail. - **Model Positioning**: Adjust clothes and dresser placement by moving pieces closer or higher to fit the frame correctly. - **Fabric Transparency**: To adjust fabric transparency to zero (fully transparent), replace sleeves or use a new fabric piece; this ensures better rendering results. - **Folded Shirt Creation**: Folded shirts are created directly from molds in the software. Version 6.0 is recommended for enhanced features (available on the official website). Different fabrics can be applied, and collars can be fixed using needles and thread for realistic folds. - **Clothing File Management**: Save clothing designs as files for reuse; folded shirts and other items can be placed on tables or shelves for display. --- ## Creating Furniture Pieces: Tables, Pillars, Shelves, and Mirrors This section covers three methods to create basic furniture components such as tables, pillars, and mirrors using Close3D, emphasizing customization of shapes, materials, and placements. ### Table and Pillar Construction - **Method 1: Direct Modeling** Create a round table, adjust edges for roundness, flatten edges to the ground, and adjust curve thickness. Pillars are cylinders with a thickness of 180 units (1.8 meters), which can be assigned metal materials and colors. - **Method 2: Using OBJ Components** Create a board, convert it to an OBJ file, import the OBJ back into the scene as a component, and adjust its width and diameter to form pillars or table parts. - **Method 3: Using Built-in 3D Shape Files** Use virtual models from the Emeta folder (e.g., 0.3 for pillars, 0.2 for virtual models). Adjust rotation and axis positions to fit the design. ### Mirror Creation - **Mirror Dimensions**: Typical mirror size used is 80 cm by 1.8 meters. - **Frame Design**: Create slim frames with rounded corners and circular edges using square and circular boards. - **Materials**: Use metal materials on the mirror and frame for realistic light reflection. Metal material must be assigned for proper reflectivity. - **Support Frame**: Construct support frames and base plates similar to pillar construction; use world coordinates for accurate placement.

Metal material must be assigned for proper reflectivity. - **Support Frame**: Construct support frames and base plates similar to pillar construction; use world coordinates for accurate placement. - **Rendering Optimization**: Assign black metal materials to increase rendering speed and visual quality. --- ## Window Display Construction and Texturing This section details building a complete window display frame, including outer edges, trims, and texturing techniques for realistic presentation. - **Frame Dimensions**: Window frame width is about 4 meters; height is 1 meter; width extends to 5 meters. - **Building Process**: - Construct outer edges by copying and rotating boards without tilting or bending. - Add top and bottom trims using boards and adjust rendering thickness for proper edge closeness. - Include inside trims for structural detail. - **Texture Application**: - Use PNG format textures for all fabrics and surfaces. - Enlarge textures as needed and apply shiny materials to add glossiness. - Apply textures on separate small boards beneath main boards to ensure correct layering. - **Additional Elements**: - Add rods and fabric for curtains (though not recommended for pulling curtains on window displays). - Add shoe cabinets or shelves with plastic materials that are slightly transparent, applying textures accordingly. - **Shadow and Lighting**: - Adjust shadow strength and texture dilution for realistic effects. - Use software-generated hairlines and other fine details automatically. - **Logo and Stickers**: - Add logos or stickers on frames by creating separate layers with thickness and placing textures accordingly. --- ## Clothing Model Adjustment and Posing Focuses on editing virtual clothing models and adjusting poses using Close3D features for realistic presentation. - **Joint Editing**: - XR joints allow editing of model bones; seven bones on each leg are locked in direction and rotation to maintain realism. - Use shortcut keys (e.g., Shift+JRX) to visualize overall concave shapes and skin surface. - Adjust leg and hand angles carefully to avoid breaking bones. - **Model Posing**: - Save adjusted poses for reuse to speed workflow. - Open saved poses to apply to models instantly. - **Simulation**: - Enable clothing simulation after pose adjustment for realistic fabric behavior. - Lower clothing quality before adjusting poses to improve speed and avoid slowdowns. - **Software Versions**: - Version 6.0 offers powerful new features; version 5.2 is slower for pose adjustments. - Download the latest version from the official website (3w.close3d.com). --- ## Materials and Rendering Techniques This section discusses material assignments and rendering tips for various components including mirrors, glasses, hats, and accessories. - **Mirror Reflection**: - Assign metal materials to mirror surfaces for proper reflections. - Adjust transparency and bleaching to control reflectivity; full bleaching (transparency set to zero) allows better mirror effects.

full bleaching (transparency set to zero) allows better mirror effects. - **Sunglasses and Glasses**: - Made from film materials applied on OBJ models. - Adjust transparency to create realistic lenses. - **Hats and Accessories**: - Construct hats from flat boards and rotate to shape. - Assign fabric materials matching the design. - Use separate OBJ files or components for accessories such as bags and necklaces. - Fix accessories with virtual needles to maintain position during simulation. - **Plastic Materials**: - Used for shoes, hands, and other props. - Slightly transparent plastic materials enhance realism. - **Texture Management**: - PNG textures are standard for all fabrics and surfaces. - Adjust texture size, dilution, and glossiness for optimal appearance. - **Lighting**: - Add multiple types of lights (sphere, laser, square, IES, skylight) for scene illumination. - Use board materials with light properties for additional effects. --- ## Advanced Display Elements: Butterflies, Curtains, and More This section explores adding decorative elements such as butterflies and curtains to enhance window displays and clothing presentations. - **Butterflies**: - Available in the software library as ZPSC files, ready to use. - Position and sew butterflies onto clothing using fake sewing tools without affecting fabric cleanliness. - **Curtains**: - To be covered in detail in future live streams. - Typically added by attaching fabric textures to rods; however, pulling curtains in window displays is not recommended. - **Layering and Transparency**: - Use layered fabrics with adjusted transparency to avoid texture conflicts and freezing issues during simulation. - **Clothing Hanging Techniques**: - Convert clothing into OBJ files to move and place items in rows on virtual racks. - Use fixed needles to position items precisely. --- ## Software and Community Resources Information on software versions, official websites, and community engagement for further learning and assistance. - **Software Versions**: - Close3D 6.0 is the latest release with enhanced functions and is available for download at [3w.close3d.com](https://3w.close3d.com). - Version 5.2 remains in use but is slower for some operations. - **Official Website**: - Contains computer configuration requirements, live streaming schedules, prize notifications, and help resources. - **Community Interaction**: - Users can join live streams, participate in lucky draws via WeChat official accounts, and access gift bags. - Q&A sessions during live streams address user questions and provide interactive demonstrations. - **Learning Resources**: - Previous live streams are available as playback for detailed tutorials. - Official accounts provide updates and downloadable assets. --- ## Summary This lesson provides comprehensive guidance on using Close3D software to create and display 3D apparel models with realistic furniture, textures, and lighting.
